key_insight: Fine image detail does not need every image token to communicate globally. SpecSlot separates globally coordinated image structure from locally modeled detail, aiming to increase detail without expanding costly global attention.
problem_solved: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically assign one token to each image patch. Capturing finer detail requires more tokens, making global attention increasingly expensive.
method: Introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space Transformer trained with rectified flow.
Use global information exchange for low-frequency structure, such as overall layout and broad shapes.
Model high-frequency detail locally to decouple output detail from global communication demands.
impact: This approach could make detailed pixel-space image generation more computationally efficient. The provided abstract is truncated, so performance gains and implementation details cannot be verified.
visual_elements: Split image showing low-frequency structure beside high-frequency textures and edges.
Side-by-side attention diagrams: dense global patch connections versus global structure exchange with local detail connections.
Conceptual pipeline: pixel input → global structure modeling + local detail modeling → generated image.
Token-grid illustration showing how finer patches increase the burden of conventional global attention.
paper_title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
paper_authors: Jiongfan Yang, Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Ziwei Liu
